description:
STRENGTH DECIDES CARRIER DUELS, AND A BRACED PLAYER HOLDS HIS GROUND. ONE BYTE. (This spec replaces tools/data/patches/duels-physical.json, which described the SAME byte and got its headline effect BACKWARDS. Everything below has been re-emulated. If you still have duels-physical.json, ignore it.)

WHAT THE BYTE DOES. 0x144310ea0 returns each player's SHARE of the separation push when two bodies overlap - a LOW share means he holds his ground, a HIGH share means he gets shoved. It has two formulas. If neither player is the ball holder or his team's pass target, it uses the full model. The moment a DRIBBLER is involved, a chain of tests at 0x14431145d-0x14431148c routes the duel to a compressed fallback at 0x14431148e that is just PCb/(PCa+PCb). This patch turns the 'je' at 0x14431145b into a 'jmp', skipping those tests so EVERY duel, carrier included, uses the full model.

WHAT THE FULL MODEL ACTUALLY IS - a-EMULATED, re-derived from the bytes and run under Unicorn on the tail 0x144311566-0x14431171c with synthetic players:
    share_A = 0.5 - 0.35*(sf_B - sf_A) - 0.3*(1 - 0.5*|sf_B - sf_A|) * clamp(PC_A - PC_B, +/-30)/30
PC is attribute 0x29 (Physical Contact, 40-99 scale; base 40.0 at 0x14431116f, fetched with r8d=0x29 at 0x1443111a1). sf is a SPEED FACTOR built at 0x14431165b-0x1443116c8 as KE = 3.6*v^2, sf = 0 below KE 5, ramping to 1.0 at KE 13.5.

THE TWO CORRECTIONS THAT MATTER, BOTH DEMONSTRATED:
 1. THE ADVERTISED EFFECT WAS BACKWARDS. The momentum term displaces the FASTER-CLOSING player MORE, so a stationary, braced carrier becomes HARDER to barge off, not easier. Emulated, the exact scenario the old spec promised - a PC 90 centre-half closing on a PC 70 forward shielding the ball while stationary - stock fallback gives share_forward = 0.5625 at every closing speed; with this patch it is 0.7000 at 0 km/h, 0.6527 at 5 km/h, then 0.3333 at 8 and 0.2500 at 12/20/28 km/h. Any defender arriving at a realistic speed shoves a set, shielding forward LESS THAN HALF as far as stock. Do not expect this patch to let you bump dribblers over; expect the opposite.
 2. THERE IS NO CONTINUOUS 'MOMENTUM'. sf saturates at 1.0 by 6.97 km/h and is 0 below 4.24 km/h, so it is effectively a binary 'is he moving'. Because the term is 0.35*(sf_B - sf_A), two players both above jogging pace CANCEL EXACTLY. Emulated, equal strength: both at 3.6, 5.4, 7.2, 10.8, 20.0 and 30.0 km/h all return exactly 0.5000, i.e. identical to stock. A dribbler running at 18 km/h against a defender sprinting at 25 or 30 km/h: 0.5000, unchanged. The only live speed case is one player essentially standing, and it protects him. (The old spec's km/h column was also mislabelled - it fed v = kmh/6 instead of kmh/3.6, so every speed in it was 0.6x what it said.)

SO WHAT IS THIS PACK FOR? Two honest things. (a) STRENGTH now decides carrier duels instead of the compressed ratio, capped at +/-0.3 over a +/-30-point PC window: emulated, both stationary, stock -> patched, 80v70 0.4667 -> 0.4000, 90v60 0.4000 -> 0.2000, 99v40 0.2878 -> 0.2000, 99v70 0.4142 -> 0.2100. A strong player is meaningfully harder to move. (b) A BRACED, STATIONARY player wins body contact against a moving one, which is a real football behaviour (shielding) even though it is not the one that was advertised.

AGAINST THE BRIEF? Partly, and you should know that before you test it. Your brief is tighter, more physical conditions that force awkward contacts. Effect (a) helps. Effect (b) works AGAINST it: shielding the ball gets EASIER for whoever is standing still. This is the one pack in this set whose net direction on your brief is genuinely uncertain, which is why it is last.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE, symmetrically - you carrying and defending, your AI team-mates, the CPU. Both players run their own copy and the two shares were verified to sum to exactly 1.000000 in three configurations.

NEW BEHAVIOUR TO WATCH FOR THAT STOCK CANNOT PRODUCE: the stock fallback PC_B/(PC_A+PC_B) is strictly bounded to 0.288-0.712 on the 40-99 scale. The full model reaches exactly 0.000000 and exactly 1.000000 at the corners (PC difference +/-30 with one player moving), so one body can now absorb 100% of the separation. If you see players sliding or snapping off each other on contact, that is this. NOT YET ESTABLISHED: what the caller's exact '== 1.0' test at 0x1441098f8 branches to.

STRUCTURAL SAFETY - b-VERIFIED, and worth stating because it is the usual risk of a control-flow edit. 0x14431149e is ALREADY reached directly by the stock 'je' at 0x14431145b with identical register state, because nothing executes between them; turning the je into a jmp therefore cannot introduce uninitialised state. The skipped block only does cmp/je plus two calls to the getter 0x1442d7090. Same length, same target, next instruction boundary preserved at 0x14431145d. Site byte-identical in PRISTINE and the INSTALLED image (7441). Division by zero in the abandoned fallback becomes unreachable from this path.

CALL SITES: 0x144310ea0 has THREE callers - 0x143ea5734, 0x1441098f0 and 0x14410c5b5. Only the 0x1441098f0 path was traced (the caller at 0x144109963 does accum += separationAxis * overlap * share). The patched branch is inside the shared callee, so it changes all three; 0x143ea5734 sits in a different subsystem and was not inspected.

NOT INCLUDED: the strength saturation window (0x14431156e / 0x144311576, 30 -> 20 points), which is the existing UNAPPLIED spec tools/data/patches/phys-duel-strength.json and touches different bytes. Judge this one first.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/duels-strength.json

patches.name: force every duel down the full strength+speed model (je -> jmp)
patches.note: je 0x14431149e -> jmp 0x14431149e. Same length, same target; only the opcode changes. Site byte-identical in PRISTINE and the installed exe. Skips the ball-holder / pass-target tests at 0x14431145d, 0x144311462, 0x144311472 and 0x144311485, so the PCb/(PCa+PCb) fallback at 0x14431148e is no longer reached from this path. The full model reads only state the function already loads, so nothing new can fault.
